title: Soft-isolation KV reallocator and prefill latency prober
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Design and implement a soft-isolation KV pool reallocator that reduces hard evictions by rebalancing slot reservations across tenant pools and workload classes. The system will integrate with kernel-selection hints and a lightweight prefill latency prober that runs synthetic prefill checks before eviction decisions. Goal: reduce tail prefill/decode regressions when contention occurs while preserving throughput for high-priority tenants.
acceptance_criteria: Rebalancer performs non-destructive slot transfers between tenant pools for at least 90% of contention events under synthetic load
Prefill latency prober detects a 10% degradation in p95 prefill latency with fewer than 5% false positives in controlled experiments
End-to-end p95 prefill+decode latency does not regress by more than 5% for production traces after rollout in canary region
Feature guarded by runtime flag and an operator-level kill-switch
Corresponding unit and integration tests and a simulation harness are checked into the repo
suggested_approach: Instrument existing KV occupancy and kernel suitability signals into a single scoring pipeline (occupancy, touch-frequency, kernel-compatibility, tenant-priority)
Implement soft-isolation state: reservations that are convertible (soft-reserves) vs hard-reserves; soft reserves are migratable with copy-on-access semantics
Add a light-weight prefill-latency prober that executes short prefill traces using representative kernels to measure realistic prefill cost before eviction decisions
Expose a reallocator controller that proposes moves; moves are staged on-device and only committed once prefill probe metrics pass thresholds
Integrate with kernel-selection so the reallocator biases placement toward shards that match preferred kernel categories to avoid kernel-mismatch penalties
tradeoffs: Increases controller complexity and CPU overhead for prefill probing vs fewer full evictions and cold decodes
Soft-migration may temporarily use extra memory while copies are staged, risking increased peak memory under extreme pressure
Favoring kernel-compatibility improves average latency but can reduce cross-tenant sharing that benefits utilization
Probing adds synthetic load; must be rate-limited to avoid interference with production traffic
test_plan: Unit tests for scoring pipeline and soft-reserve state transitions
Simulation harness that replays production allocation/eviction traces and measures successful non-destructive migrations
Controlled cluster-level integration: enable feature in a canary shard, run mix of synthetic and sampled production traces, measure p50/p95 prefill+decode
Chaos test: induce sudden memory pressure and ensure controller respects operator kill-switch and falls back to hard-evict behavior
Benchmark: compare kernel-mismatch-rate and end-to-end token throughput vs baseline
rollout_plan: Start with internal test cluster (dev) for 72h
Canary rollout to one region and 5% of requests for 1 week
Gradual increase to 25% then 100% while monitoring metrics and aborting on thresholds
Post-rollout 2-week observation window with retention of detailed traces for root-cause analysis
